reading: Every plus-shaped pattern of colour-0 cells (a 0 cell whose four orthogonal neighbours are also 0) is recoloured 3, overlapping pluses included; everything else stays.

new_rows.name: plus0
new_rows.datalog:
pc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), Y1 = Y - 1, px(Y1, X, 0), Y2 = Y + 1, px(Y2, X, 0), X1 = X - 1, px(Y, X1, 0), X2 = X + 1, px(Y, X2, 0).
plus0(Y, X) :- pc(Y, X).
plus0(Y2, X) :- pc(Y, X), Y2 = Y - 1.
plus0(Y2, X) :- pc(Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1.
plus0(Y, X2) :- pc(Y, X), X2 = X - 1.
plus0(Y, X2) :- pc(Y, X), X2 = X + 1.

why: exactly the cells of 0-pluses change, each 0 -> 3 (background is 8 in some pairs and 0 in others, so px is used, not cell)

reading: A single marker on a uniform grid; a colour-1 path runs vertically through the marker's column (skipping the marker) from top to bottom edge, then turns along the top edge to one corner and along the bottom edge to the opposite corner (Z/S shape).

slots.line: marker column, full height, colour 1, marker kept
slots.top_arm: top row from marker column to one corner (left in pairs 0 and 2, right in pair 1)
slots.bottom_arm: bottom row from marker column to the opposite corner
slots.side_choice: unclear; fits marker-row parity (odd row -> top arm goes left)

why: output = input plus a 1-path from one top corner to the opposite bottom corner whose vertical leg is the marker column

reading: The loose objects (the colour that is neither background nor the fixed floor/wall structure) fall straight down as rigid objects, stacking on each other, and stop with exactly one background cell between them and the floor or bottom edge.

slots.subject: objects of the non-background, non-floor colour
slots.stop: one cell above the floor structure / bottom edge (gap of 1); a falling object stacks directly on an already-landed one
slots.floor: the large fixed structure of another colour (walls/posts/base)

why: each object keeps its shape; its lowest cells end with exactly one background cell above the floor; floor never changes

reading: One full row is a two-colour template; each other row holds only a prefix of the template in other colours. Each partial row is completed by copying the template's pattern with the template colours replaced by that row's colours (mapping read from the prefix).
verb: complete rows from template with colour substitution

slots.key: per row: template colour at each prefix position -> row colour there

why: every completed row equals the template under a per-row colour bijection consistent with its prefix

reading: The single marker moves down one cell; then every cell above the moved marker's row in columns of the same parity as the marker's column becomes 4.
verb: drop marker and draw comb above

new_rows.name: comb
new_rows.datalog:
col(X) :- cell(MY, MX, C), X = MX.
col(X2) :- col(X), X2 = X + 2, px(0, X2, V).
col(X2) :- col(X), X2 = X - 2, px(0, X2, V).
comb(Y, X) :- cell(MY, MX, C), col(X), px(Y, X, 0), Y < MY.

why: the marker shifts by (+1,0); afterwards 4 fills exactly rows < marker row in columns congruent to the marker column mod 2

reading: Several rectangular pieces each carry holes/patterns; the output is the largest piece with smaller pieces nested into it wherever a piece's pattern matches that piece's hole pattern (recursively: a piece nested in another can itself receive a smaller piece).

slots.base: the largest piece, cut out as the output canvas
slots.placement: each insert is pasted where its inner-colour cells line up with the host's hole cells of that colour
slots.order: largest host first, then smaller inserts into inserted pieces

why: output size = largest piece's box; every other piece appears once, aligned so its marked cells coincide with the host's marked cells

reading: A frame of four 4-corners with two coloured side bars and a separate two-colour shape; the output is the frame box with the shape placed inside, mirrored left-right if needed so each colour sits next to the side bar of the same colour.

slots.canvas: bounding box of the 4-cornered frame with its side bars
slots.orientation: identity or horizontal flip, whichever puts each colour beside its matching bar

why: output = frame box; interior = shape (possibly flipped) whose left colour equals left bar colour and right colour equals right bar colour

reading: Every hole inside a rectangular outline is filled by size: one-cell holes become 5, two-cell holes become 7.

new_rows.name: hole1
new_rows.datalog:
nb(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
hole1(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), Ya = Y - 1, nb(Ya, X), Yb = Y + 1, nb(Yb, X), Xa = X - 1, nb(Y, Xa), Xb = X + 1, nb(Y, Xb).

new_rows.name: hole2
new_rows.datalog:
nb(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
hh(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), X2 = X + 1, px(Y, X2, 0), Xa = X - 1, nb(Y, Xa), Xb = X + 2, nb(Y, Xb), Ya = Y - 1, nb(Ya, X), nb(Ya, X2), Yb = Y + 1, nb(Yb, X), nb(Yb, X2).
vv(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), Y2 = Y + 1, px(Y2, X, 0), Ya = Y - 1, nb(Ya, X), Yb = Y + 2, nb(Yb, X), Xa = X - 1, nb(Y, Xa), nb(Y2, Xa), Xb = X + 1, nb(Y, Xb), nb(Y2, Xb).
hole2(Y, X) :- hh(Y, X).
hole2(Y, X2) :- hh(Y, X), X2 = X + 1.
hole2(Y, X) :- vv(Y, X).
hole2(Y2, X) :- vv(Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1.

why: only enclosed background cells change; size-1 holes -> 5, size-2 holes -> 7

reading: Two vertical bars (colours 2 and 4) appear above and below a separator line; the output is a 2x2 block of the colour whose bar grew more from the top panel to the bottom panel.

slots.panels: top and bottom stripes cut by the 5 separator row
slots.measure: per colour: cell count below minus cell count above

why: winner colour has the larger (bottom - top) count difference on every pair

reading: Each 2x2 block of colour 2 has four diagonal corner cells of different colours; the corner colours rotate one step clockwise around the block, then each corner shoots a diagonal ray of its new colour outward to the grid edge.
verb: rotate corner colours and shoot diagonal rays

slots.unit: each 2x2 block with its four diagonal corner markers
slots.rays: from each corner diagonally away from the block until the border, in the corner's new colour
slots.crossings: rays of different blocks may cross; precedence unclear

why: 2x2 blocks unchanged; corner cells permuted clockwise; diagonal rays outward carry the corner's new colour
